title: Narrative Systems Engineering: Signal-Grounded Multimodal Metrics and State-Space Control Dynamics for Audiovisual Media
description:
Foundational research framework, mathematical formalization, and reproducible C#/.NET 10 multimodal computational engine (Argon.Engine v0.4) originated by Jair Ivan Rojas Ruiz (ORCID: 0009-0003-1109-4583; foundational archive September 8, 2026) for measuring, modeling, identifying, and controlling audiovisual narratives as coupled acoustic, visual, and linguistic signals u(t) acting on a bounded cognitive-social state space x(t+1) = f(x(t), u(t)).

Includes formal operationalization of the six core NSE metrics: Narrative DNA (signed entity-belief tripartite graphs), Narrative Entropy (Shannon bits), Narrative Energy (cross-modal prosodic-visual-linguistic resonance functional), Narrative Complexity, Narrative Inertia, and Narrative Controllability (discrete-time Controllability Gramian W_c), validated across a 3-work cross-domain benchmark corpus (EXP-001, EXP-002 Phase-Space Atlas, EXP-003 6! = 720 Counterfactual Montage Optimization, and EXP-004 Tikhonov Ridge Inverse System Identification & LOCO Generalization).

Terminology Disambiguation & Chronological Priority: This work (archived since September 8, 2026) formally establishes the quantitative, signal-grounded, and state-space discipline of Multimodal Narrative Systems Engineering and Computational Narrative Dynamics (NSE/CND), explicitly distinct from homonymous qualitative or essayistic uses of the phrase (such as game-design blogs or Strangium's November 2, 2026 NSE-001 qualitative screenplay taxonomy) that lack mathematical formulations, signal processing, state-space models, or executable software.
notes: Originated, authored, and directed by Jair Ivan Rojas Ruiz (ORCID: 0009-0003-1109-4583). Repository: https://github.com/jaiborojas-cloud/narrative-systems-engineering
